review.notes: Text lineage is cosmetic throughout, and trailing, so it is recorded here rather than as a change entry: v0 (FET-EN011, 2005-03-01) -> v1 (DR3-EN131, 2006-11-25) rewrites 'an Effect Monster that is destroyed by this monster as a result of battle' to 'an Effect Monster that this card destroyed by battle' and 'as a result of battle' to 'by battle'. The EARTH negation branch is unchanged behaviourally: the only diff lines touching it are RESET_EVENT|RESETS_STANDARD_EXC_GRAVE vs RESET_EVENT+RESETS_STANDARD_EXC_GRAVE, the same value written two ways. The battle-destruction timing doctrine sits next to the period rule profile's damage-step structure, but no rule-profile flag can make a card listen to a different event code, so it is a per-card ruling; upstream shipping a per-card variant solely for it supports that reading.

event.historical_text: This monster gets the following effect(s) while there is a monster(s) with the following Attribute(s) on the field:●EARTH: Negate the effect of an Effect Monster that is destroyed by this monster as a result of battle.●WIND: If this card destroyed your opponent's monster as a result of battle, it can attack once again in a row.
event.summary: Era trigger timing, not a text erratum: the GOAT script registers the WIND 'attack once again in a row' optional trigger on EVENT_BATTLED and re-checks the battle afterwards (Duel.GetAttacker()==this card, the attack target is the opponent's and IsBattleDestroyed()), where the modern script fires on EVENT_BATTLE_DESTROYING via aux.bdocon at the instant of destruction. Upstream annotates the variant 'Battle destroyed registers while the mosnter is on field'; the behavioural content is when the optional trigger's window opens and therefore whether it can miss timing. Chronology of this procedural change is unresolved - nothing in the packet or in chronologies.json bounds it.
